title: Orbit rollout coordinator for LTS sync and soft-drain
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Build and ship the 'Orbit' rollout coordinator: a release-time controller that synchronizes LTS channel rollouts across heterogeneous GPU slices while minimizing tenant impact through a negotiated autoscaler handshake and soft-drain semantics. This task implements the controller, upgrades the upgrade-runbook, and adds telemetry and dashboards required to validate safe capacity preservation during live rollouts.

Background / Motivation: We have frequent churn when performing LTS upgrades across Dedicated GPU pools: bursty evictions, autoscaler thrash, and tenant SLA blips. Existing controllers either drain too fast (causing pressure and higher latency) or too slow (delays rollout). Orbit's intent is to provide a deterministic pace for upgrades tied to autoscaler capacity contracts, tenant admission pacing, and pre-warmed buffer slices. This reduces observed latency spikes and lowers the risk of failed rollouts requiring rollbacks.

Design summary:
- Coordination handshake: Orbit negotiates a window with the cluster autoscaler by registering a 'soft-evict token' for a GPU slice subset. The autoscaler responds with an admission budget (tokens per-minute) and indicates when pre-warm buffer is required.
- Soft-drain semantics: Instead of immediate eviction, Orbit marks pods as 'soft-drain' which permits existing sessions to finish per configurable grace windows and prevents new tenant admissions on affected slice(s). New requests are routed to alternative pools using smart routing rules.
- Tenant-aware pacing: Tenants flagged as latency-sensitive (via tenant metadata) get longer drain windows and are scheduled onto reserved buffer capacity first. Less-sensitive tenants are preempted earlier.
- Heterogeneous slice handling: Orbit groups devices by capability (memory, compute, quant-friendly variants) and performs version tiling so compatible model variants are used as fallbacks.
- Canary+Gate system: Every rollout passes through 'canary window' (small fraction of devices), 'ramp window' (controlled expansion), and 'drift window' (observability hold) gates. Gates are automatic but pause on SLO regressions above thresholds.
- Telemetry & safety: Emit granular events for token negotiation, per-slice admission budgets, estimated remaining capacity, and tenant fallback counts. Add per-rollout dashboard with latency, 99th percentile token wait times, and admission denial rate.

Acceptance criteria:
- Orbit can perform a full LTS channel upgrade on a test fleet (mixed A100/V100 equivalent slices) with no more than 5% increase in p95 latency and no increase in error rate across tenant traffic compared to baseline.
- No more than 2% of tenants see interrupted sessions (as measured by session aborts) during a projected 6-hour upgrade window.
- Controller exposes a rollout-trace ID; runbook steps can use it to find linked events, PRs, and metrics dashboards.
- Autoscaler handshake documented and integration tests covering token grants/denials completed.

Implementation plan:
1) Controller PoC (2 weeks): implement soft-evict API, token negotiation stub, slice grouping logic. Add unit tests.
2) Integration with autoscaler (2 weeks): implement handshake, admission budget handling, and pre-warm trigger. Add integration tests running against a local autoscaler simulator.
3) Tenant routing & model fallbacks (1 week): implement smart routing to route blocked admissions to compatible model variants or alternative pools.
4) Safety gates + observability (1 week): add gate logic, metrics emission, and basic dashboard templates.
5) Staged rollout + runbook update (1 week): run internal canary, collect results, iterate on pacing parameters.

Runbook highlights (for on-call):
- How to abort: issue 'cancel-rollout' via Orbit API which transitions soft-drains to immediate admission open.
- Emergency rollback: if gate fires due to >10% p95 degradation, automatically pause and revert devices in the previous LTS tile.
- Recovery: if autoscaler disconnects, Orbit falls back to conservative fixed-window draining (configurable) and emits high-severity alert.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Autoscaler misreports capacity causing overcommit. Mitigation: conservative safety multiplier and pre-warm verification probes before admitting traffic.
- Risk: Tenant metadata missing or inaccurate. Mitigation: default to conservative (latency-sensitive) behavior and add tooling for tenant metadata backfill.
- Risk: Model-variant incompatibilities causing fallback failures. Mitigation: preflight compatibility matrix check and staged canary using synthetic prompts.

Need to tighten admission budget smoothing to reduce token bursts. Test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/rollout/orbit-load-2026-03-01
